result.summary: This PR is a full end-to-end implementation of Erlay (BIP 330), adding dedicated low-bandwidth 'outbound-full-reconciliation' connections that a node falls back to for transaction relay if it suspects it is being eclipsed on its normal connections. It implements the reconciliation handshake, sketch construction/decoding, extension rounds, eviction and connection-accounting changes, new protocol messages, and extensive new tests/benchmarks. The author explicitly marks it '[DO NOT MERGE]': its purpose is to validate the design end-to-end before splitting it into smaller PRs for real review.
result.problem: Bitcoin's current transaction relay (flooding to all peers) wastes bandwidth and, more importantly, an eclipsed node can be starved of transaction announcements if an attacker controls all its connections; Erlay adds set-reconciliation-based relay to give a bandwidth-cheap fallback channel that is harder to fully eclipse. Node operators with limited bandwidth and the wider network's censorship/eclipse resistance are the intended beneficiaries.

open_concerns: Whether OUTBOUND_FULL_RECONCILIATION should count as a full-outbound connection for eviction/seeding purposes (author went ahead with 'yes' but invites reconsideration)
Whether sketch extensions are worth keeping now that reconciliation is a fallback rather than the primary relay path
A malicious peer sending a maximal sketch can force ~2.3s (8.8s with extension) of single-threaded decode time, a potential DoS vector (brunoerg), not yet mitigated by capacity limits
Whether reconciliation should be negotiated via BIP-434 instead of repurposing sendtxrcncl
A possible race allowing one extra reconciliation connection during v2-to-v1 transport downgrade (brunoerg), noted but deferred by author
resolved_concerns: BIP330 success-byte parsing nit (must be 0/1) - fixed by author to mirror BIP152 handling
Author addressed most of brunoerg's mutation-testing coverage gaps for the non-extension path with new unit/functional tests

result.card: This is a full, explicitly 'DO NOT MERGE' implementation of Erlay (BIP 330) bandwidth-efficient transaction relay, adding new low-bandwidth 'outbound-full-reconciliation' connections as an eclipse-resistance fallback for tx propagation. It solves a long-standing, tracked problem (issue #30249): a node can be starved of transaction announcements if all its connections are captured by an attacker, and reconciliation gives a cheap redundant channel. The author states it exists to validate the whole design before splitting it into smaller reviewable PRs, and several core design questions remain open, including whether reconciliation connections count as full-outbound and whether a maximal sketch's ~2.3-8.8s decode time is an acceptable DoS surface (raised by brunoerg, unresolved). The PR needs a rebase, is marked dirty/conflicting with six other open PRs, and is under active, ongoing rework by the author as recently as September 2026. Reviewing this specific diff is of limited direct value since it will be superseded by the planned split, but the underlying Erlay work is strategically significant for the p2p/eclipse-resistance category.
